items.text:
A size advantage in heading persistence can coexist with multiple active regions.

overall interpretation: H1 is inconclusive, H2 fails the declared overall gate and H3 is inconclusive in both arms and all seven views, with
forced states shown separately. No model satisfies all H1 requirements (three required); only Holmes meets the main H2 model criterion (two
required). The multiple-region predictor has Spearman +0.091 and 0/4 successful sign folds; count has−0.389 and 3/4, with one unavailable fold
each. Neither reaches the required negative association magnitude 0.6. No eligible distinct H3 mode pair satisfies the complete
corroboration/fingerprint conjunction. The chosen main figure instead reports the robust f = 0.05 observation in Wave-pinning, Holmes and
Spring, with the full four-model overview alongside it. This is a conditional polarity result, not support for universal noise buffering or a
validated multiplicity predictor.

retained qualifications: Finite-window bounds, unavailable comparisons and unbounded intervals remain explicit. Across all 185 conditions,
each arm has 156 passing,17 failing and 12 inconclusive descriptive window checks. For the 52 preselected extended conditions, each view has
50 passing and 2 inconclusive horizon checks; the original-cohort check has the same counts. These are sensitivity qualifications, not
additional hypothesis gates or equivalence proofs. At the selected input, all three-model size-ratio CIs remain above 1 in all seven views;
selected endpoint persistence/regime window checks pass. Native regimes and fixed-physical smoothed/downsampled imaging proxies stay distinct.
Global-heading physical mobility is a proxy, literal single-region site MSD is separate, and neither establishes cell migration. Historical
Spring sampling failures and original/repaired/E4 Gaussian-lineage accounting remain in the supplement. The selected f = 0.05 conditions were
not preselected for E4 extension. Both selector tables reuse the same common-horizon observations here; they are one cohort, rather than
independent long-horizon confirmation.

Wave-pinning

pattern: At f = 0.05, the large/small heading-persistence ratio is 4.44 (95% CI 3.20–9.07). The primary optical large-cell multiple-region
time fraction is 60.1% (51.1–69.3%), versus 3.4% in small cells. Size-dependent heading persistence therefore coexists with multiple observed
regions.

numeric shortfalls: H1 has 5 supported gains among 11 evaluable inputs, but no complete model pass. Its f½ CIs overlap: common
small[0.0001,0.03], large[0.0001,0.1]; longest small[0.0001,0.02], large[0.0001,0.05]. H2 has no qualified reversal/drop range. H3 shows the
multiple-region class, without a qualified distinct second class.

qualifications: The f = 0.05 size advantage survives all seven views and both arms. Late-quarter persistence is bounded, with an unbounded CI
endpoint. Its direct geometry-normalized persistence CI includes 1; the global-heading physical-mobility proxy increases and is a separate
short-lag estimand.

Goryachev

pattern: Non-forced weak-input heading persistence remains censored. At f = 0.05 the large-cell native low-contrast fraction is 90.0%, while
usable-pair coverage for persistence is 0.131, below 0.5. Those observations stay visible, with the operational forced-state flag.

numeric shortfalls: H1 has 0 supported direct-ratio gains among 5 evaluable non-forced inputs and unbounded overlapping f½ CIs. H2 has no
qualifying non-forced range. Goryachev supplies the candidate contrast-loss class for H3, but forcing/coverage qualification and the full
distinct-class fingerprint conjunction do not pass.

qualifications: Forced-inclusive results remain separate. A numerical ratio computed from the remaining valid pairs does not establish an
eligible persistent heading. The unmatched f = 0.015 designed endpoint and its missing comparison remain explicit.

Holmes 3

pattern: At f = 0.05 the heading-persistence ratio is 2.74 (95% CI 2.20–3.47); the primary optical large-cell multiple-region fraction is
83.0% (79.5–85.9%), versus 9.8% in small cells. The same multiple-region class appears under strong input.

numeric shortfalls: H1 has 4 supported gains among 11 evaluable inputs; f½ CIs overlap (common small[0.0001,0.02], large[0.0001,0.03]; longest
both[0.0001,0.02]). H2 passes for this model in main:2.228-fold drop from f = 0.03 to 0.3. Overall requires at least 2 models, and the primary
count predictor ρ = −0.389 falls short of−0.6 by 0.211.

qualifications: The conditional H2 model result becomes inconclusive in the second-half and late-quarter views. The f = 0.05 size advantage
itself survives all seven views; its late-quarter upper bound is unbounded. This distinction remains visible rather than redefining the
hypothesis after the window checks.

Spring

pattern: At f = 0.05 the persistence ratio is 1.167 (95% CI 1.093–1.251), while the primary optical large-cell multiple-region fraction is
53.0% (50.4–55.3%), versus 0.08% in small cells. The count increase is therefore compatible with a modest positive heading-persistence size
effect.

numeric shortfalls: H1 has 7 supported gains among 10 evaluable inputs, with overlapping f½ CIs: small[0.0001,0.003], large[0.0001,0.01]. The
f = 1 reversal, ratio 0.877 (0.785–0.976), is operationally forced and cannot support the non-forced H2 call. H3 corroborates the same
multiple-region class, not an eligible distinct second class.

qualifications: Use the measured changing circumference: the actual geometric ratio at f = 0.05 is 8.534, rather than the resting-size
reference 9. Historical sampled-duration/cadence failures remain explicit; successful native replay does not establish all region-lifetime or
duration convergence.

pages.label: S0_memo_06_01
pages.title: Interpretation and alternative framings · Persistence and global-heading mobility respond differently to enlargement.

items.text:
Persistence and global-heading mobility respond differently to enlargement.

supporting panels: S4/S5 geometry and mobility, S12 cadence checks, and the same f = 0.05 small/large native comparisons. At that input,
global-heading-derived physical-mobility ratios are 1.845,3.606 and 6.356 in Wave-pinning, Holmes and Spring, each withCI above 1, alongside
persistence ratios above 1.

weaknesses: The global-heading conversion is not one tracked site diffusivity. Short-lag slopes are cadence-sensitive; Wave-pinning direct
excess-persistence CI includes the geometric reference, so the two source estimands cannot be collapsed into a strict common geometric claim.

further runs: Save finer scalar output and test converged short-lag slopes at the same fixed inputs; extend qualified single-region tracks to
compare literal site MSD with the heading-derived proxy. No new integrations are included in this delivery.

pages.label: S0_memo_07_01
pages.title: Interpretation and alternative framings · Model-dependent loss of a single persistent polarity pattern.

items.text:
Model-dependent loss of a single persistent polarity pattern.

supporting panels: Full S2 regime/coverage maps, S7 fixed-mean sigma sweeps, S9 optical fingerprints and S0 H3 component/pair tables; the all-
model main overview can lead this framing.

weaknesses: Only the multiple-region class is qualified and corroborated across the eligible models. Goryachev contrast loss is
forced/undercovered, and no distinct eligible pair passes the full fingerprint test. A descriptive difference cannot be promoted to a
confirmed mechanism-specific failure law.

further runs: Sample additional fixed-mean Goryachev transition inputs with mean controls and sigma contrasts to seek an abnormal state with
adequate heading coverage, then predeclare and retest the distinct-class fingerprints. Longer weak-input runs would also tighten the currently
overlapping noise-tolerance bounds.
